# Public holidays, school terms and daylight saving ## On this page - [Public holidays in the ACT](https://www.act.gov.au/living-in-the-act/public-holidays-school-terms-and-daylight-saving#Public-holidays-in-the-ACT) - [ACT public school term dates](https://www.act.gov.au/living-in-the-act/public-holidays-school-terms-and-daylight-saving#ACT-public-school-term-dates) - [Subscribe to iCalendar](https://www.act.gov.au/living-in-the-act/public-holidays-school-terms-and-daylight-saving#Subscribe-to-iCalendar) - [Daylight saving in the ACT](https://www.act.gov.au/living-in-the-act/public-holidays-school-terms-and-daylight-saving#Daylight-saving-in-the-ACT) ## Public holidays in the ACT The next public holiday is Friday 25 December 2026 Christmas Day Public holidays in Australia are different in each state and territory. These are the ACT’s public holidays. ### 2026 | Public holiday | Date | | --- | --- | | New Year's Day | Thursday 1 January | | Australia Day | Monday 26 January | | Canberra Day | Monday 9 March | | KB\]](https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0017/3003713/ACT-Public-Holidays-2029.pdf) ### Bank holidays The _[Holidays Act 1958](https://www.legislation.act.gov.au/a/1958-19)_ includes bank holidays. In the ACT, there is a bank holiday on the first Monday in August. Bank holidays do not apply to everyone. Refer to your Enterprise Agreement or Award for more information. ## ACT public school term dates These are term dates for our public schools. Private schools may have different dates. ### 2026 | Term | Student start date | Term end date | | --- | --- | --- | | Term 1 | New students\*: Friday 30 January
Continuing students: Monday 2 February | Thursday 2 April | | Term 2 | Tuesday 21 April | Friday 3 July | | Term 3 | Tuesday 21 July | Friday 25 September | | Term 4 | Tuesday 13 October | Friday 18 December | [2027 public school term dates](https://www.act.gov.au/living-in-the-act/public-holidays-school-terms-and-daylight-saving#) | Term | Student start date | Term end date | | --- | --- | --- | | Term 1 | New students\*: Monday 1 February


Continuing students: Tuesday 2 February | Friday 9 April | | Term 2 | Wednesday 28 April | Friday 2 July | | Term 3 | Tuesday 20 July | Friday 24 September | | Term 4 | Tuesday 12 October | Friday 17 December | \*New students include anyone starting at a school for the first time or transitioning to the next school type. This includes: - all Kindergarten students (even if they previously attended the attached preschool) - all year 7 students (even if they previously attended the school as a primary school student) - all year 11 students (even if they previously attended the school as a high school student) - students in any year level who are starting at the school for the first time (please confirm with your school about timing and requirements on the first day). College exam periods are managed and communicated by individual schools. Please contact your school for more information. ### Download public school term calendars - [2026 ACT public school term dates \[PDF 349 KB\]](https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0004/2992693/2026-ACT-public-school-term-date-calendar-.pdf) - [2026-2030 ACT public school term dates \[PDF 118 KB\]](https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0005/2827589/ACT-school-term-dates-2026-30-web-print-friendly.pdf) - [2026-2030 ACT public school term dates \[DOCX 47 KB\]](https://www.act.gov.au/__data/assets/word_doc/0006/2827590/ACT-public-school-term-dates-2026-30-web-print-friendly.docx) ## Subscribe to iCalendar Find out how to add dates to your device by [subscribing to iCalendar](https://www.act.gov.au/living-in-the-act/public-holidays-school-terms-and-daylight-saving/icalendar). ## Daylight saving in the ACT Daylight saving in the ACT is the same as in New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Tasmania. ### Start and end dates Daylight saving begins at 2am Eastern Standard Time on the first Sunday in October each year. This is when you need to put your clocks forward one hour. Daylight saving ends at 3am Eastern Daylight Saving Time on the first Sunday in April. This is when you need to put your clocks back one hour. In 2026, daylight saving starts at **2am on Sunday 4 October 2026.** This page is managed by: [Chief Minister, Treasury and Economic Development Directorate](https://www.act.gov.au/directorates-and-agencies/chief-minister-treasury-and-economic-development-directorate) Last updated: 14 August 2026 ![](https://fonts.gstatic.com/s/i/productlogos/translate/v14/24px.svg) Original text Rate this translation Your feedback will be used to help improve Google Translate reCAPTCHA
